title: Geneva canton housing market
subtitle: Official OCSTAT transactions · two different price units
tech_line: OCSTAT · Python · DuckDB · extract → transform → validate

kpi.mid_caption: City of Geneva · existing PPE · free market · 2024

01_ppe_trend.title: Existing apartments: median CHF/m² doubled since 2006
01_ppe_trend.note: Source: OCSTAT T 05.05.1.4.03 · Existing PPE, free market, canton · Band = P25–P75

02_city_vs_canton.title: City of Geneva has stayed above the canton PPE median
02_city_vs_canton.note: Existing PPE, free market, annual. City premium = city median / canton median − 1. Latest: +{premium_pct}%.

03_ppe_map.title: Apartments (PPE) in 2024: CHF/m² only where OCSTAT publishes a median
03_ppe_map.note: Grey = no median (n<10 or not in the table), not zero. Residual Autres groups not mapped. City of Geneva = four sectors, one colour.

03b_map_apartments.title: Apartment prices per m² by commune
03b_map_apartments.subtitle: Canton of Geneva · Existing apartments (PPE) · CHF/m² · Free market · 2024
03b_map_apartments.note: Source: OCSTAT T 05.05.1.4.03 · Notarial transactions · Grey = n<10 (unpublished) · City of Geneva = four sectors combined

03c_map_houses.title: House prices by commune
03c_map_houses.subtitle: Canton of Geneva · Detached houses · Median CHF per dwelling · 2024
03c_map_houses.note: Source: OCSTAT T 05.05.1.3.03 · Notarial transactions · Grey = n<10 (unpublished) · Not CHF/m²

04_ppe_range.title: Existing apartment prices vary 1.8× across communes
04_ppe_range.subtitle: Canton of Geneva · Existing apartments (PPE) · CHF/m² · Free market · 2024
04_ppe_range.note: Source: OCSTAT T 05.05.1.4.03 · P25–P75 range · YoY % vs 2023 · Unpublished communes (n<10) omitted

04c_new_vs_existing_commune.title: Within each commune, new apartments cost 17–29% more
04c_new_vs_existing_commune.subtitle: Canton of Geneva · CHF/m² · Free market · 2024 · Only communes with both segments
04c_new_vs_existing_commune.note: Source: OCSTAT T 05.05.1.4.03 · Median CHF/m² · Canton-level “existing > new” reversal = Simpson’s paradox (composition effect)

04b_ppe_range_new.title: New apartments: only 5 communes have enough data
04b_ppe_range_new.subtitle: Canton of Geneva · New apartments (PPE) · CHF/m² · Free market · 2024
04b_ppe_range_new.note: Source: OCSTAT T 05.05.1.4.03 · P25–P75 range · YoY % vs 2023 where available · Unpublished = n<10

05_premium_vs_canton.title: Vs the canton: City premium, Vernier the steepest published discount
05_premium_vs_canton.note: Existing PPE, free market, 2024. Premium = commune median / canton median − 1. Canton benchmark at 0%. Author's calculations.

06_ppe_new_vs_existing.title: New apartments are not automatically more expensive per m² than existing apartments
06_ppe_new_vs_existing.note: Apartments in condominium ownership (PPE), free market, canton, annual medians. Quarterly CHF/m² does not exist — do not splice object prices onto this chart.

06b_apartments_2024_quartiles.title: Existing apartments cost more per m² than new ones
06b_apartments_2024_quartiles.subtitle: Canton of Geneva · CHF/m² · Free market (PPE) · Annual 2024
06b_apartments_2024_quartiles.note: Source: OCSTAT T 05.05.1.4.03 · P25–P75 range, free market · YoY % vs 2023

07_new_build_premium.title: New-build premium vs existing apartments has changed sign, not a stable markup
07_new_build_premium.note: Canton, free market, annual. Premium = median_new / median_existing − 1. Historical comparison only — not a buy-new vs buy-existing recommendation. Author's calculations.

08_price_vs_cagr.title: Current level vs {cagr_years}-year CAGR — two different questions
08_price_vs_cagr.note: Source: OCSTAT T 05.05.1.4.03 · Existing PPE, free market · CAGR = annualised growth · Author's calculations

09_q_latest_avg_ticket.title: New vs existing: average transaction value across four segments
09_q_latest_avg_ticket.subtitle: Canton of Geneva · Average ticket (value / n), not median · Quarterly — the only frequency with new vs existing
09_q_latest_avg_ticket.footnote: Source: OCSTAT T 05.05.1.1.01 · YoY % vs same quarter prior year · House average skewed by premium communes

10_volume_activity.title: Transaction counts: apartments remain the larger market; existing stock dominates later charts
10_volume_activity.note: Canton, annual ensemble counts (new + existing). n is activity, not a direct liquidity measure. Do not plot n on the same axis as CHF/m².

11_volume_new_existing.title: Turnover mix: existing dwellings account for most observed sales
11_volume_new_existing.note: Canton, annual. New vs existing composition. New vs existing CHF/m² exists only for PPE, annual — not this chart.

12_quarterly_pulse.title: Quarterly pulse: counts and ticket size — not CHF/m²
12_quarterly_pulse.note: Canton. Activity = ensemble n. Price = existing dwellings, CHF per object (OCSTAT 1.1.02). PPE quarterly prices are not CHF/m² and are not spliced onto the annual m² series.

13_house_ticket.title: House ticket size: published communes, not a price per living-space m²
13_house_ticket.note: Detached houses, 2024, median with P25–P75. OCSTAT does not publish living-space CHF/m² for houses. Do not compare this axis with PPE CHF/m².

14_q_latest_existing_range.title: House prices show 2× wider dispersion than apartments
14_q_latest_existing_range.subtitle: Canton of Geneva · CHF per transaction (not per m²) · Existing stock only
14_q_latest_existing_range.note: Source: OCSTAT T 05.05.1.1.02 · P25–P75 range, existing stock · YoY % vs {prev_q}

15_price_vs_n.title: Same-cell n: some high apartment medians rest on few observed sales
15_price_vs_n.ylabel: Transactions in the same OCSTAT cell (n)
15_price_vs_n.note: Existing apartments (PPE), free market, 2024. n is fact_price.n for the same commune/year/filter — not canton volume. Small n: treat the median as a thin sample. Author's calculations.

17_market_shocks.title: Year-on-year changes around 2008, 2020 and 2022 — association, not causes
17_market_shocks.note: Canton, annual. Vertical markers = calendar years often discussed, not identified shocks. The chart does not prove interest-rate or COVID causality. Author's calculations.

18_libre_vs_zd.title: Apartments in development zones have lower medians than the free-market ensemble
18_libre_vs_zd.note: Canton, annual, condition = ensemble (all) for both series so only market differs. Libre and ZD are different regimes — do not blend into one “market price”.

19_budget_area.title: At a CHF {budget} budget, implied floor area differs sharply by commune
19_budget_area.xlabel: Implied m² = budget / median CHF per m²
19_budget_area.note: Theoretical benchmark only: Budget / published existing-PPE free-market median, 2024. Not predicted apartment size; ignores unit quality, fees, financing and whether such dwellings transacted. Author's calculations.

21_quarterly_corridor.title: Quarterly prices: stable corridor, no sustained decline
21_quarterly_corridor.note: Source: OCSTAT T 05.05.1.1.02 · Existing dwellings, canton · Band = P25–P75 · Q1 2007 – Q2 2026

20_houses_trend.title: Detached houses (all): median per dwelling tripled since 1990
20_houses_trend.note: Source: OCSTAT T 05.05.1.3.03 · All detached houses, canton · Band = P25–P75 · Not CHF/m²

callout: Compare apartments in CHF/m² and houses in CHF per dwelling. Do not put them on one CHF axis.
conclusions: In 2024, existing PPE on the free market: canton {canton_m2} CHF/m², City of Geneva {city_m2} (+{premium_pct}%).
Among {n_communes} communes with a published median the range is wide: {top_commune} {top_m2} to {bottom_commune} {bottom_m2} CHF/m² — not a 45-commune choropleth.
Houses in 2024: median {house_m} million CHF per dwelling; the canton does not publish living-space CHF/m².
Turnover 2024: houses {h_ex} existing vs {h_new} new; PPE {p_ex} existing vs {p_new} new.
New PPE median {new_m2} CHF/m² vs existing {canton_m2} in 2024 ({new_prem_pct}% new-build premium).
footer: Source: OCSTAT T 05.05 / SITG CAD_COMMUNE. Missing values not interpolated. Derived metrics marked as author's calculations. Code: GitHub.
